Actual Article Body:
A federal judge has ordered White House access to journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico to be restored, saying U.S. President Donald Trump's ban was likely unconstitutional.

In his ruling, District Judge Tim Kelly said the three outlets should have their access immediately restored from the ban that the president had announced on Sept. 18. The judge had been nominated by Trump to the federal bench in 2017.

Kelly said the Trump administration must return, reinstate and restore the White House "hard pass" press credentials held by employees of the three outlets that had been revoked. The order is set to remain in effect for 14 days.

"Simply put—the record lacks factual support for Defendants' contention that the revocation of Plaintiffs' hard passes will in fact protect national security or that national security will be endangered if the Court orders their passes reinstated while this litigation proceeds," Kelly said.

US District Judge Tim Kelly issued his order in a lawsuit that the news organisations filed contesting the ban, which the Republican president announced on September 18.
